tests.why: Her four highest fasting mornings each follow a day she barely ate. Aug 11 'only water today except coffee' -> Aug 12 morning 9.0. Aug 14 'ate lightly, not hungry' -> Aug 15 8.7. Aug 18 'have not eaten yet, sore gut' -> Aug 19 8.5. Aug 19 cottage cheese and pork rinds -> Aug 20 9.6, the record. The mornings after a real early supper (Jul 31, Aug 2, Aug 10) all behaved. Under-eating plus pain plus inflammation drives cortisol and glucagon, and both tell the liver to make glucose. Weight fell 142.2 to 139.0 in three days and resting pulse hit a record 82 over the same window.
tests.success: A real supper eaten by 6:30 every day for seven days. If the fasting rolling-5 falls back under 8.0 without any change to what she eats, the driver is intake, not content or timing.

closed.verdict: NEGATIVE. The dose step never happened. It was an arithmetic error.
closed.evidence: The counter is a RUNNING DAILY TOTAL, so the day's dose is the last non-zero row of that day. Every day from Aug 1 to Aug 19 reads 1300mg or less. There is no day above 2 pills anywhere in the record. The 1950 and 2600 figures came from adding the last value of the midday session to the last value of the evening session. The evening rows are the same running total being re-tapped, not a second dose. 1300mg/day in a 75-year-old is well under half the usual ceiling, so there is no glutathione argument at that dose. Do not reopen without a day that actually reads above 1300mg.

traps: TIME: timeLocal is her wall clock. The ISO timestamp is 2 hours ahead of America/Vancouver because her device sits at UTC-5. stamp() builds both from the device. Her own typed times (Jul 22 'about 10:00 pm' on a 10:41 PM row, Jul 24 '8;00 pm' on an 8:01 PM row, Jul 26 '12:00' on a 12:24 PM row, Jul 27 '9:00 pm' on a 9:13 PM row) prove timeLocal is the real one. Use timeLocal for everything. Never convert the ISO field.
FOOD: a food row's time is when she pressed save, NOT when she ate. The meal log has an eat-time field that lands in the row as '· ate 7:30'. When it is there it wins.
COUNTERS: Tylenol, magnesium and gummy tiles are running daily totals. Last non-zero row of the local day IS the day's dose. Never add sessions.
